data.summary: The Cartesian plane uses perpendicular x- and y-axes meeting at the origin (0, 0). Points, midpoints and distances are the basic tools.
key_concepts: A point is written (x, y); the origin is (0, 0)
Read scales carefully: each small square may represent 1 unit or a fraction of a unit
Distance between two points comes from Pythagoras on the coordinate differences
Midpoint is the average of the x-coordinates and of the y-coordinates

formulas.label: Distance
formulas.note: Same as length of the line segment joining the points.

worked_examples.question: A point is 4 units left of the origin and 7 units above it. State its coordinates.
steps: Left of the origin means negative x
Above the origin means positive y

worked_examples.question: Find the distance between A(3, -5) and B(-1, -9).

common_mistakes.mistake: Subtracting coordinates when finding a midpoint.
common_mistakes.fix: Midpoint means average: add and divide by two.

common_mistakes.mistake: Misreading the grid scale when plotting or reading a point.
common_mistakes.fix: Check what each small square represents before reading coordinates.

exam_tips: Always label the x-axis and y-axis on sketches.
Plot points roughly to sanity-check distance and midpoint answers.
